0BSD.summary: Zero-Clause BSD grants permission to use, copy, modify and distribute the software with or without a fee. The inspected grant is unconditional on retention of a copyright notice.

copyright_grant.text: The grant covers use, copying, modification and distribution for any purpose with or without a fee.

notices.text: The inspected grant has no retention condition. This observation applies to this text.

patent_grant.text: The reviewed text does not expressly address contributor patent rights.

warranty.text: The text states warranty and liability disclaimers.

scenarios.situation: Packaging code labeled BSD
scenarios.text: Check the exact identifier and instrument. The source and binary notice conditions in other BSD editions do not establish a notice condition in the 0BSD grant.

AGPL-3.0-only.summary: AGPLv3 governs copying and conveying covered works and includes a source offer for qualifying remote interaction with a modified program.

copyright_grant.text: Section 2 grants permission to run the unmodified program and addresses making, running and propagating covered works that are not conveyed.

modification.text: Conveying a covered work in modified source form has change-notice and licensing conditions.

network_interaction.text: If the modified version supports remote network interaction, it must prominently offer remotely interacting users access to its Corresponding Source at no charge.

notices.text: Verbatim source conveyance must follow the license-copy and notice requirements. Modified source is subject to further notice conditions.

patent_grant.text: Section 11 defines an express patent grant from contributors for their essential patent claims over their contributor versions.

source_availability.text: Conveying object code requires use of an applicable Corresponding Source mechanism. Installation Information applies in specified User Product transactions.

termination.text: Section 8 provides for termination for specified noncompliance and circumstances for provisional or permanent reinstatement.

scenarios.situation: Operating a modified network service
scenarios.text: Determine whether users interact remotely with the modified program and how those users can obtain Corresponding Source under the offer. Assess any copying of client code or appliances separately.

scenarios.situation: Applying AGPLv3 to a new project
scenarios.text: Use the correct license copy and application notices that specify the actual edition and later-version choice.

Apache-2.0.summary: Apache License 2.0 provides explicit contributor copyright and qualified patent grants. Redistribution has license-copy and notice conditions, with additional treatment of modified files and a relevant upstream NOTICE.

copyright_grant.text: Subject to the terms, contributors grant the specified reproduction, derivative-work, display, performance, sublicensing and distribution rights in source or object form.

modification.text: Modified files must carry prominent notices of changes when redistributed under §4.

notices.text: Give recipients a license copy. Retain pertinent upstream copyright, patent, trademark and attribution notices in any derivative Source you distribute. When the Work was distributed with a NOTICE file, include readable pertinent attribution from that file in distributed Derivative Works using a location specified in §4(d).

patent_grant.text: Subject to the license terms, each contributor grants the specified patent rights over the Work. The grant covers only claims that contributor can license and that their contribution necessarily infringes by itself or in combination with the Work to which they submitted it.

termination.text: If you institute patent litigation against any entity, including a cross-claim or counterclaim, alleging that the work or an incorporated contribution directly or contributorily infringes a patent, the §3 patent licenses for that work terminate as of the filing date.

source_availability.text: Section 4 permits redistribution of the Work and Derivative Works in Source or Object form under its stated conditions. Section 4(c) governs notice retention in any derivative Source distributed.

trademark.text: Section 6 withholds permission to use the Licensor’s trade names, trademarks, service marks or product names, with a stated exception for reasonable and customary descriptions of the Work’s origin and reproduction of NOTICE content.

warranty.text: Section 7 supplies the Work from the Licensor and Contributions from their respective contributors on an as-is basis. Section 8 separately limits contributor liability to the recipient. Both sections have applicable-law and written-agreement qualifications.

scenarios.situation: Shipping a modified binary
scenarios.text: Give recipients a copy of the license and check that modified files carry prominent change notices. Inspect any accompanying derivative Source for pertinent upstream notices. For a distributed Derivative Work whose upstream distribution included a NOTICE file, check for readable pertinent attribution in a location permitted by §4(d). How a specific binary package carries the modified-file notices requires separate review.

scenarios.situation: Applying Apache-2.0 to a new project
scenarios.text: Keep the publisher license copy, including the appendix, intact. The ASF’s own-software guidance discusses personalizing a separate source-file notice, an alternative copyright line with the SPDX identifier, and consideration of a NOTICE file.

sources.locator: How should I apply the Apache License to my own software?

BSD-2-Clause.summary: This BSD form permits use and redistribution with notice conditions for source and binary forms.

copyright_grant.text: The instrument permits use and redistribution in source or binary form, with or without modification, subject to its conditions.

notices.text: Retain the copyright notice, conditions and disclaimer with distributed source. Reproduce them in documentation or accompanying materials when distributing binaries.

patent_grant.text: The reviewed text has no separately stated patent grant.

warranty.text: The closing paragraphs disclaim stated warranties and limit liability.

scenarios.situation: Distributing a binary package
scenarios.text: Carry the notice, conditions and disclaimer in documentation or other materials supplied with the distribution.

BSD-3-Clause.summary: This BSD form permits use and redistribution with notice conditions and restricts use of holder and contributor names for endorsement.

copyright_grant.text: The instrument permits use and redistribution in source or binary form, with or without modification, subject to its conditions.

endorsement.text: The holder’s and contributors’ names may be used to endorse or promote derived products only with specific prior written permission.

notices.text: Retain the copyright notice, conditions and disclaimer with distributed source. Reproduce them in documentation or accompanying materials when distributing binaries.

patent_grant.text: The reviewed text has no separately stated patent grant.

warranty.text: The closing paragraphs disclaim stated warranties and limit liability.

scenarios.situation: Distributing a binary package
scenarios.text: Carry the notice, conditions and disclaimer in documentation or other materials supplied with the distribution.

scenarios.situation: Preparing marketing material
scenarios.text: Retaining attribution and representing developer endorsement are separate issues. Inspect the proposed use of names against clause 3.

BUSL-1.1.summary: The Business Source License 1.1 uses project-specific parameters. Its initial use terms are replaced by a stated Change License at the earlier of the specified date or the version-specific anniversary in the text.

copyright_grant.text: The initial grant lists copying, modification, derivative works, redistribution and non-production use.

future_license.text: The Change License takes effect at the earlier of the Change Date or the fourth anniversary of first public distribution of that specific version under the license.

production_use.text: Production use can fall within a separately specified Additional Use Grant. Review the actual project text and scope.

scenarios.situation: Deploying a particular release
scenarios.text: Read the actual release terms, including the Additional Use Grant and Change Date. Verify the date of first public distribution for that version.

CC-BY-NC-4.0.summary: CC BY-NC 4.0 grants specified use of copyright and similar rights for NonCommercial purposes. Sharing is subject to attribution conditions.

commercial_use.text: The grant is limited to NonCommercial purposes as defined in §1. Applicability depends on the purpose of the use.

copyright_grant.text: The grant covers reproduction and sharing of the licensed material and production, reproduction and sharing of adapted material for NonCommercial purposes.

database_rights.text: Section 4 addresses extraction, reuse, reproduction and sharing under Sui Generis Database Rights.

notices.text: Sharing requires retaining the applicable identifying, copyright, license and disclaimer information and indicating modifications as specified.

scenarios.situation: Reusing a software manual
scenarios.text: Identify whether code samples share the manual’s license. Analyze the purpose of the use and which attribution information accompanies the copied material.

sources.locator: Can I apply a Creative Commons license to software?

CC-PDM-1.0.summary: The Public Domain Mark communicates a determination about existing copyright status. SPDX lists it as a related instrument.

copyright_grant.text: The mark communicates known copyright status. It does not perform the function of a grant by a rights holder.

jurisdiction.text: Copyright status can vary by jurisdiction. Creative Commons recommends using the mark for works free of known copyright worldwide.

sources.locator: Recommended Uses of the Public Domain Mark

marking.text: Creative Commons describes it as a label for works free of known copyright worldwide.

sources.locator: Recommended Uses of the Public Domain Mark

scenarios.situation: Marking an archival work
scenarios.text: Check territorial copyright evidence behind the marking and separately consider other rights in the work.

sources.locator: Recommended Uses of the Public Domain Mark

CC0-1.0.summary: CC0 is a public-domain dedication that attempts a waiver and supplies a fallback license when applicable. Its scope covers defined copyright and related rights.

copyright_grant.text: To the stated extent that the waiver is ineffective, the affirmer grants a fallback license in the listed rights.

dedication.text: The affirmer waives specified Copyright and Related Rights to the extent permitted by applicable law.

patent_grant.text: The instrument expressly leaves the affirmer’s patent rights unaffected.

third_party_rights.text: The affirmer disclaims responsibility for clearing others’ rights. Ownership and third-party claims require their own evidence.

trademark.text: The instrument expressly leaves the affirmer’s trademark rights unaffected.

scenarios.situation: Dedicating project material
scenarios.text: Identify which rights the affirmer controls and the scope of the material. Check separately for relevant patents, trademarks or third-party rights.

CDDL-1.0.summary: The CDDL grants rights in Covered Software and applies source and notice conditions to its distribution. The edition matters for precise grant and termination language.

copyright_grant.text: The initial developer and contributors grant specified non-patent and non-trademark intellectual property permissions under §2, subject to §3.1 and third-party claims.

notices.text: Preserve listed notices and provide the CDDL copy accompanying covered source.

patent_grant.text: The patent grants have distinct scope and exclusions for the initial developer and subsequent contributors.

source_availability.text: Making Covered Software available in executable form triggers a source availability obligation and information on obtaining the source.

termination.text: Section 6 describes breach and patent-claim termination, with specified timing and survival of some end-user licenses.

scenarios.situation: Shipping a Larger Work containing CDDL code
scenarios.text: Determine which components are Covered Software and which changed files are Modifications before planning source access and notice handling.

CDDL-1.1.summary: The CDDL grants rights in Covered Software and applies source and notice conditions to its distribution. The edition matters for precise grant and termination language.

copyright_grant.text: The initial developer and contributors grant specified non-patent and non-trademark intellectual property permissions under §2, subject to §3.1 and third-party claims.

notices.text: Preserve listed notices and provide the CDDL copy accompanying covered source.

patent_grant.text: The patent grants have distinct scope and exclusions for the initial developer and subsequent contributors.

source_availability.text: Making Covered Software available in executable form triggers a source availability obligation and information on obtaining the source.

termination.text: Section 6 describes breach and patent-claim termination. Section 6.3 also addresses certain patent-related settlements before patent litigation.

scenarios.situation: Shipping a Larger Work containing CDDL code
scenarios.text: Determine which components are Covered Software and which changed files are Modifications before planning source access and notice handling.

Classpath-exception-2.0.summary: This exception permits a specified combination with independent modules when applied by the relevant copyright holders to the base license.

exception_relationship.text: Inspect the project’s grant for the relevant library, including the GPL version election and any required file designation. GNU Classpath 0.95’s Package.java and OpenJDK jdk-25+36 illustrate distinct project notices.

linking_permission.text: The grant permits linking the covered library with independent modules and copying and distributing the resulting executable under chosen terms, subject to the terms of each linked independent module. The definition of independence excludes a module derived from or based on the library.

modification.text: The grant lets a modifier extend the exception to their version of the library. It directs a modifier who chooses to omit it to remove the exception statement from that version.

standalone_installation.text: The exception supplies additional permission for a base-license relationship and refers to the covered library and its project notices.

scenarios.situation: Distributing an executable using the exception
scenarios.text: Verify the library’s actual grant and the terms and independence of each linked module. For Oracle’s exception in OpenJDK jdk-25+36, compare the express designation in Object.java with the java.cpp header, which lacks that designation. Check modified copies separately.

EPL-1.0.summary: EPL 1.0 grants contributor copyright and patent rights under stated terms and provides requirements by distribution form.

copyright_grant.text: The contributor grants the listed copyright permissions concerning its contribution and covered derivative works, subject to the agreement.

notices.text: Include a copy of the agreement with each source copy, retain copyright notices and identify each contribution’s originator.

patent_grant.text: The contributor patent grant applies to the defined Licensed Patents, with limitations for combinations.

source_availability.text: The agreement permits object-code distribution under other terms subject to conditions including a statement of source availability and an explanation of how to obtain it.

scenarios.situation: Shipping object code under separate terms
scenarios.text: Review the alternate agreement’s disclaimers, source availability statement and instructions. Check copyright and contribution-origin notices.

EPL-2.0.summary: EPL 2.0 grants contributor rights with source availability and notice conditions. A Secondary License route has specific combination and notice requirements.

copyright_grant.text: The contributor grants the listed copyright permissions concerning its contribution and covered derivative works, subject to the agreement.

notices.text: Preserve the categories of notices named in §3.3 and include a copy of the agreement with source distributions.

patent_grant.text: The contributor patent grant applies to the defined Licensed Patents, with limitations for combinations.

secondary_license.text: The §3.2(a) route depends on the combination with material in separate files under a Secondary License and the initial Contributor’s Exhibit A notice.

source_availability.text: Distribution of the Program requires making source available and communicating how recipients can obtain it.

scenarios.situation: Using the Secondary License route
scenarios.text: Check the initial contributor’s notice and the arrangement and licensing of separate files. The identifier alone does not establish the necessary circumstances.

FSL-1.1-ALv2.summary: The Functional Source License 1.1 grants specified rights for Permitted Purposes, defines Competing Use and names a license available on the stated future trigger.

competing_use.text: The permitted-purpose definition excludes competing uses meeting the instrument’s terms and gives examples of permitted purposes.

copyright_grant.text: The instrument grants the listed permissions for Permitted Purposes subject to its stated terms.

future_license.text: The future-license clause names Apache License 2.0 and defines the time trigger tied to the Software.

scenarios.situation: Offering a hosted product
scenarios.text: Assess the commercial offering against the actual Competing Use definition and identify the Software version and date relevant to its future-license clause.

FSL-1.1-MIT.summary: The Functional Source License 1.1 grants specified rights for Permitted Purposes, defines Competing Use and names a license available on the stated future trigger.

competing_use.text: The permitted-purpose definition excludes competing uses meeting the instrument’s terms and gives examples of permitted purposes.

copyright_grant.text: The instrument grants the listed permissions for Permitted Purposes subject to its stated terms.

future_license.text: The future-license clause names MIT and defines the time trigger tied to the Software.

scenarios.situation: Offering a hosted product
scenarios.text: Assess the commercial offering against the actual Competing Use definition and identify the Software version and date relevant to its future-license clause.

GPL-2.0-only.summary: This SPDX identifier describes a grant restricted to GNU GPL version 2. The project's authorized license notices establish where that grant applies.

copyright_grant.text: The text allows verbatim copying and distribution and permits modified distributions subject to §§1–2.

modification.text: Section 2(a) requires prominent notices of changes and their dates in modified files. Section 2(b) applies to distribution or publication of a work containing or derived from the Program and requires licensing the work as a whole under GPLv2 at no charge to third parties. Section 2 separately addresses independent works distributed separately and mere aggregation.

notices.text: For verbatim source distribution, §1 requires appropriate copyright and warranty-disclaimer notices on each copy, retention of the license and no-warranty notices, and a copy of GPLv2 for recipients.

source_availability.text: For object code or executables, §3(a) provides for accompanying complete machine-readable corresponding source on a customary medium under §§1–2. Section 3(b) provides for an accompanying written offer valid for at least three years to supply the source to any third party at up to the distributor's physical source-distribution cost. Section 3(c) allows passing along the received offer information only for noncommercial distribution after receiving the binary with a compliant §3(b) offer.

termination.text: Section 4 makes attempted unauthorized copying, modification, sublicensing or distribution void and automatically terminates the actor's GPLv2 rights. Downstream parties who received copies or rights under the license retain their licenses while in full compliance.

version_choice.text: An explicit version 2 only grant limits the recipient to that version. Check the authorized notice or other grant for the relevant files and release. Section 9 has a separate rule for a program covered by a GNU GPL grant that omits the version number.

scenarios.situation: Acquiring a GPLv2 codebase
scenarios.text: Inspect the actual copyright holder's license declaration for the exact project version and component. Use the shared GPLv2 document to read version 2 terms and the authorized declaration to establish the permitted version choices.

scenarios.situation: Offering a GPLv2 executable for download
scenarios.text: When the executable is distributed through copy access from a designated place, §3 counts equivalent copy access to the corresponding source from the same place as distributing the source. Check the required license and notices under §§1–2 and the scope of corresponding source under §3.

GPL-2.0-or-later.summary: This SPDX identifier describes a grant allowing the recipient to follow GNU GPL version 2 or a later FSF version. The following distribution terms describe the version 2 election.

copyright_grant.text: The text allows verbatim copying and distribution and permits modified distributions subject to §§1–2.

modification.text: Under GPLv2, §2(a) requires prominent notices of changes and their dates in modified files. Section 2(b) applies to distribution or publication of a work containing or derived from the Program and requires licensing the work as a whole under GPLv2 at no charge to third parties. Section 2 separately addresses independent works distributed separately and mere aggregation.

notices.text: For verbatim source distribution under GPLv2, §1 requires appropriate copyright and warranty-disclaimer notices on each copy, retention of the license and no-warranty notices, and a copy of GPLv2 for recipients.

source_availability.text: Under GPLv2, §3(a) provides for accompanying complete machine-readable corresponding source on a customary medium under §§1–2. Section 3(b) provides for an accompanying written offer valid for at least three years to supply the source to any third party at up to the distributor's physical source-distribution cost. Section 3(c) allows passing along the received offer information only for noncommercial distribution after receiving the binary with a compliant §3(b) offer.

termination.text: Section 4 makes attempted unauthorized copying, modification, sublicensing or distribution void and automatically terminates the actor's GPLv2 rights. Downstream parties who received copies or rights under the license retain their licenses while in full compliance.

version_choice.text: Where the applicable grant specifies version 2 or any later version, §9 permits following version 2 or a later GPL version published by the FSF. An applicable GNU GPL grant with no version number uses the separate rule in §9.

scenarios.situation: Acquiring a GPLv2 codebase
scenarios.text: Check the copyright holder's declaration for the exact release and component. When the grant permits a later edition and you elect it, use that edition's terms for the covered conduct.

scenarios.situation: Redistributing a received executable under GPLv2
scenarios.text: To pass along the received source-offer information under §3(c), confirm that the redistribution is noncommercial and that you received the executable or object code with a compliant §3(b) offer. If either condition is absent, assess the applicable alternatives in §3(a) and (b).

GPL-2.0-with-classpath-exception.summary: SPDX deprecates this composite identifier and records separate replacement guidance for the identifier and for a legacy expression with a trailing plus. Check the original grant when applying either SPDX expression to a file.

identifier_status.text: This identifier remains listed as deprecated in SPDX 3.29.0.

replacement_guidance.text: The bare identifier’s recorded replacement is GPL-2.0 WITH Classpath-exception-2.0. Applying SPDX’s separate replacement for the bare GPL-2.0 base yields GPL-2.0-only WITH Classpath-exception-2.0. The legacy trailing-plus expression maps directly to GPL-2.0-or-later WITH Classpath-exception-2.0.

application_scope.text: Confirm the base-version election and the exception in the notice covering the actual file. GNU Classpath 0.95’s Package.java declares GPL version 2 or later with the Classpath exception.

scenarios.situation: Migrating a legacy Classpath identifier in an SPDX document
scenarios.text: Preserve the original token and whether it carried a plus. Record the SPDX replacement path separately from the licensing conclusion for each component. Check original license notices before recording a version election or changing a file-level declaration.

sources.locator: Source header, base election and exception

GPL-3.0-only.summary: GPLv3 provides copying and modification permissions. Conveying covered works carries requirements that depend on the form and circumstances of the transfer. The only identifier refers to a version 3 declaration.

copyright_grant.text: Section 2 permits running the unmodified Program and making, running or propagating covered works without conveyance while the license remains in force. A separate conveyance permission for exclusive outsourced work or running facilities has conditions on license compliance, direction, control and copying outside that relationship.

modification.text: Conveying modified source under §5 requires prominent notices of changes and a relevant date, a license notice, and licensing the covered work as a whole under GPLv3. Section 5 separately defines when co-packaged independent works form an aggregate.

network_interaction.text: Mere network interaction without transfer of a copy is outside §0’s definition of conveyance. Assess any copies actually transferred. Section 13 separately addresses a qualifying combination with AGPLv3-covered work.

notices.text: Section 4 requires copyright and other specified notices and a license copy for recipients of verbatim source. Section 5 adds changes and date notices and a qualified interactive-interface requirement. Section 6 carries §§4–5 into object-code conveyance.

patent_grant.text: Section 11 grants a nonexclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license under each contributor’s essential patent claims for the contents of that contributor’s version. The definition excludes claims infringed only as a consequence of further modification.

source_availability.text: Conveying object code requires machine-readable Corresponding Source for the covered work through an applicable §6 route. Installation Information is a separate obligation for specified User Product transfers, subject to the exception when neither the conveyor nor any third party retains installation ability.

termination.text: Section 8 terminates rights for unauthorized propagation or modification. Upon cessation of violations, reinstatement works separately for each copyright holder. Permanent reinstatement has distinct paths for no notice before 60 days from cessation and first notice from that holder followed by cure before 30 days from receipt. Existing downstream licenses survive the termination.

version_election.text: GPL-3.0-only identifies an application of version 3 only. Inspect the licensing declaration for the material. Section 14 provides a later-version election for a declaration that expressly includes that option, and a separate rule for a declaration with no version number.

scenarios.situation: Shipping an embedded binary
scenarios.text: Evaluate the applicable Corresponding Source route for a physical shipment, offer, download or other conveyance. For Installation Information, check User Product status, a transfer of possession and use including a fixed term, and whether anyone retains the ability to install modified object code.

scenarios.situation: Applying GPL version 3 only to a new project
scenarios.text: Keep the publisher’s license document intact and declare version 3 only in the authorized project or source notice. The license appendix illustrates an or-later notice, so choose the notice wording for the intended grant.

GPL-3.0-or-later.summary: This profile covers the GPLv3 later-version election. GPLv3 terms govern when the recipient follows version 3. A later-version election requires examining the chosen version's own terms.

version_election.text: If the Program's declaration specifies GPL version 3 or any later version, §14 allows a recipient to follow version 3 or a later GPL version published by the Free Software Foundation.

notices.text: Apply the later-version election through an authorized licensing declaration. The same GNU GPLv3 document accompanies both version 3 choices. Inspect the declaration that applies to the relevant material.

scenarios.situation: Evaluating a version election in a distribution with mixed source notices
scenarios.text: Check which grant covers each relevant file or component before relying on a later-version election. An explicit version 3 or later declaration supports that choice for its covered material. Assess conflicting notices or a versionless declaration separately.

sources.locator: Copying permission statement and version declaration

ISC.summary: The ISC grant allows use, copying, modification and distribution, including for a fee, with a notice condition.

copyright_grant.text: The grant covers use, copying, modification and distribution for any purpose with or without a fee.

notices.text: The copyright and permission notices must appear in all copies.

patent_grant.text: The reviewed text does not expressly address contributor patent rights.

warranty.text: The text states warranty and liability disclaimers.

scenarios.situation: Distributing paid copies
scenarios.text: Include the copyright and permission notices in the copies. The same textual condition applies to distribution for a fee.

LGPL-2.0-only.summary: The GNU Library GPL version 2 governs distribution of the library and specified linked works with distinct source and relinking conditions.

linked_works.text: Review §6’s exact conditions for distributing a work linked with the library, including how recipients can modify and relink the library.

modification.text: Modified library distributions are subject to §2 conditions, including conditions on notices and licensing.

source_availability.text: Distributing the library in object or executable form requires accompanying corresponding machine-readable source under the stated terms.

version_choice.text: The selected SPDX identifier describes the version-only application.

scenarios.situation: Distributing an executable that links an LGPL library
scenarios.text: Record the package structure, distribution terms, available source and whether recipients can use a modified library. Apply the reviewed edition’s linked-work provisions.

LGPL-2.1-only.summary: LGPL 2.1 provides library copying and distribution permissions with source conditions and specific rules for distributing works that link the library.

linked_works.text: Review §6’s conditions for a linked work, including reverse-engineering terms and the stated choices concerning relinking or a suitable shared-library mechanism.

modification.text: Modified library distributions are subject to §2 conditions, including conditions on notices and licensing.

source_availability.text: Distributing the library in object or executable form requires accompanying corresponding machine-readable source under the stated terms.

version_choice.text: The selected SPDX identifier describes the version-only application.

scenarios.situation: Distributing an executable that links an LGPL library
scenarios.text: Record the package structure, distribution terms, available source and whether recipients can use a modified library. Apply the reviewed edition’s linked-work provisions.

LGPL-3.0-only.summary: LGPL 3.0 incorporates GPLv3 and adds permissions and requirements for specified library uses, including conveying a Combined Work.

linked_works.text: The additional permission for conveying a Combined Work is subject to notice, license-copy, reverse-engineering and relinking or suitable shared-library conditions.

notices.text: The Combined Work provisions require specified notices and copies of GPLv3 and LGPL 3.0.

source_availability.text: The Minimal Corresponding Source, application materials and installation requirements depend on the §4 option and facts of conveyance.

scenarios.situation: Bundling a program with a library
scenarios.text: Check the requirements for replacing the linked library and provide appropriate notices and both license documents. Determine what Installation Information is applicable.

LLVM-exception.summary: The LLVM exceptions modify specified Apache 2.0 terms for compiler-embedded Object code and for a defined combination with GPLv2-licensed software when the court condition applies.

exception_relationship.text: The exception accompanies Apache License 2.0 when the applicable grant includes it. SPDX represents that combination as Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception. Identify the covered material and any separately licensed third-party or legacy code in the release.

sources.locator: License statement, exception and separately licensed material

embedded_object.text: When compiling your source embeds portions of the covered software in the Object form of that source, the exception permits redistribution of those embedded portions in that form without the conditions in Apache §§4(a), 4(b) and 4(d).

notices.text: Apache §4(c) has its own trigger for pertinent notices in distributed Source-form Derivative Works. The compiler-embedded Object permission names the license-copy, modified-file notice and applicable upstream NOTICE conditions in §§4(a), 4(b) and 4(d).

sources.locator: Apache §4 and LLVM exception, embedded Object paragraph

combined_software.text: If compiled forms of the covered software are combined or linked with GPLv2-licensed software and a competent court finds an Apache section conflicts with GPLv2 conditions, the distributor may elect to waive or exclude the affected sections in full, retroactively and prospectively, solely for that combination. The text specifically names §§3 and 9.

scenarios.situation: Distributing output that embeds covered LLVM portions
scenarios.text: Identify portions embedded as a result of compiling your own source. Check the scope separately for a standalone tool or runtime shipped alongside the output, for source distributions, and for third-party parts under other terms.

sources.locator: LLVM exception and separately licensed third-party material

scenarios.situation: Linking a compiled component to GPLv2-licensed software
scenarios.text: Check the actual GPL version governing the component, the compiled combination and any competent court finding. If the trigger applies, record which complete sections the permitted election covers and which artifacts form the Combined Software.

sources.locator: LLVM Combined Software definition and conditions

MIT.summary: The MIT text grants broad permission to use, modify and distribute the software. Copies or substantial portions must include the copyright and permission notices.

copyright_grant.text: The grant lists use, copying, modification, merging, publication, distribution, sublicensing and sale.

notices.text: Include the copyright and permission notices in copies or substantial portions.

patent_grant.text: The reviewed text has no separately stated patent grant. Implied rights require separate analysis.

source_availability.text: The reviewed text specifies notice retention. It does not expressly address providing source with a binary.

trademark.text: The reviewed grant does not expressly address trademark permission.

warranty.text: The final paragraph disclaims warranties and limits liability.

scenarios.situation: Redistributing a library in a commercial package
scenarios.text: Preserve the third-party notice where the copy-or-substantial-portion condition applies. Review what material from the library ships with the package.

scenarios.situation: Applying MIT to a new project
scenarios.text: Complete year and holder fields in a reviewed application template. Retain existing notices on third-party code.

MPL-1.1.summary: MPL 1.1 permits distributing Covered Code within a larger product. Distributing its executable triggers source availability and notice conditions, including specific retention periods for electronic delivery of modifications.

copyright_grant.text: The Initial Developer grants specified rights in Original Code. Each contributor grants specified rights in that contributor's Modifications. Both grants are subject to third-party intellectual property claims and exclude patent and trademark rights from this part of the grant.

larger_work.text: You may distribute a Larger Work combining Covered Code with other code as one product if you meet the requirements for the Covered Code. A separate executable license has its own conditions, including preserving recipients' rights to the source.

modification.text: For Covered Code released as a series of files, edits to a file containing Original Code or earlier Modifications and new files containing any of that material can be Modifications. The license requires a file documenting changes and their dates for Covered Code to which you contribute.

notices.text: Include the license with distributed source, reproduce the Exhibit A notice in each source file or in a discoverable place if the file structure prevents it, and give executable recipients a conspicuous notice explaining source availability as specified.

patent_grant.text: The Initial Developer's patent grant addresses Original Code. A contributor's grant addresses that contributor's Modifications and specified combinations with the Contributor Version. The exclusions depend on the grant and cover some alterations or combinations.

source_availability.text: Make your Modifications available as source to anyone to whom you made an executable available. The source may accompany that executable or use an accepted electronic distribution mechanism. The electronic route specifies at least 12 months from first availability or at least six months after a subsequent version of that particular Modification becomes available to those recipients. You are responsible for availability through a third-party host.

termination.text: The noncompliance clause provides automatic termination if a breach remains uncured 30 days after you become aware of it. Separate patent-litigation rules distinguish the allegation, the affected grants and the applicable notice or effective date.

version_choice.text: The license contains a later-version option and separately allows the Initial Developer to designate portions for alternative licensing in their notices. The applicable source notice and the specific combination matter when evaluating an alternative license.

scenarios.situation: Shipping a modified binary from a short-lived download URL
scenarios.text: Check whether each recipient can obtain the source for the Modifications. If you use electronic delivery, account for the applicable minimum availability period and the conspicuous executable notice. An external hosting service leaves the source-availability obligation with you.

scenarios.situation: Putting copied code in a new file in a larger product
scenarios.text: When Covered Code was released as files, the new file can be a Modification if it contains part of the Original Code or earlier Modifications. A separate file containing only independently written material does not meet that criterion merely by shipping alongside Covered Code. Check the actual code and its license notices before relying on alternative terms.

MPL-2.0.summary: MPL 2.0 requires source licensing and access for covered files under specified distribution conditions. A larger work may contain separate material governed by other terms.

copyright_grant.text: Each Contributor grants the rights specified in §2.1(a) over its Contributions under rights it can license, excluding patents and trademarks. The grant takes effect for a Contribution on that Contributor’s first distribution and is subject to §§3.1–3.4.

larger_work.text: A Larger Work may be distributed on chosen terms if the distributor also meets the MPL requirements for Covered Software. Section 3.3 separately provides for additional distribution under a qualifying Secondary License where its combination and compatibility conditions hold.

modification.text: The definition of Modifications covers qualifying changed files and new source files that contain Covered Software. Distributed Covered Software source remains subject to the license.

notices.text: Preserve the substance of license notices in the Source Code Form of Covered Software. Section 3.4 allows changes to the extent required to correct known factual inaccuracies.

patent_grant.text: Section 2.1(b) grants rights over a Contributor’s Contributions or Contributor Version under that Contributor’s defined, licensable Patent Claims. The grant takes effect on the Contributor’s first distribution of the Contribution and has the exclusions in §2.3.

source_availability.text: A distributor of Covered Software in Executable Form must make the source available under §3.1 and tell executable recipients how to get the source by reasonable means, in a timely manner, for at most the cost of distribution to them.

termination.text: Section 5.1 provides automatic termination for noncompliance and separate routes to reinstatement. The patent litigation specified in §5.2 terminates both §2.1 grants from all Contributors for the Covered Software, subject to the trigger’s stated exclusions and §5.3’s surviving end-user agreements.

scenarios.situation: Shipping an executable Larger Work with an edited MPL file
scenarios.text: Make the Covered Software’s source available under §3.1 and give executable recipients the access instructions required by §3.2(a). Include new source files containing portions of Covered Software when identifying Modifications, and evaluate separate material under §3.3.

ODbL-1.0.summary: ODbL addresses rights in a database and circumstances in which notices, share-alike or access to a derivative database apply.

database_rights.text: The grant in §3 concerns the Database, subject to its terms. Rights in individual contents can be governed separately.

notices.text: Section 4 distinguishes notices for conveying the Database from notices associated with public use of a Produced Work.

share_alike.text: Public use of a Derivative Database brings the terms described in §4.4 into consideration.

source_availability.text: Public use of a Derivative Database, or a Produced Work from it, can require an offer of specified machine-readable materials.

scenarios.situation: Publishing results from a modified database
scenarios.text: Identify whether the results are a Produced Work and whether their underlying source is a Derivative Database. Examine both public-use and access conditions.

PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0.summary: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 grants copyright permission for permitted purposes and has separate clauses for distribution and changes. Its personal-use and institutional-use clauses identify different ways a purpose can qualify.

commercial_use.text: The general copyright grant and the permission to make changes or new works depend on a permitted purpose. Noncommercial purposes qualify, and two further clauses describe covered personal uses and use by specified organizations.

sources.locator: Copyright License, Changes and New Works License, Noncommercial Purposes, Personal Uses and Noncommercial Organizations

copyright_grant.text: The copyright grant covers acts that otherwise infringe the licensor's copyright in the software when done for a permitted purpose. The instrument sets out the grants for distribution and for changes or new works in separate clauses.

sources.locator: Copyright License, Distribution License and Changes and New Works License

distribution.text: The distribution clause grants permission to distribute copies, including copies with changes and new works allowed by the changes clause. Each recipient of any part must receive the stated notices. The instrument expressly bars sublicensing or transferring the licenses it grants you.

sources.locator: Distribution License, Notices and No Other Rights

notices.text: Give anyone receiving a copy of any part the terms or the specified URL, together with copies of any plain-text Required Notice lines the licensor provided with the software.

patent_grant.text: The grant covers patent claims the licensor can or becomes able to license that your use of the software would infringe.

termination.text: After first written notice of a violation, licenses can continue if you fully comply and take practical corrective steps within 32 days of receipt. A written patent claim about the software can end the patent license immediately, with a distinct scope for claims made by your company.

warranty.text: The instrument disclaims warranties and conditions and excludes the licensor's liability to the extent the law allows.

scenarios.situation: Running a grant-funded university research project
scenarios.text: Use by an educational institution is a permitted purpose under the institutional clause regardless of the funding source or obligations from that funding. Verify who uses the software. A for-profit partner's separate use requires its own assessment. An institutional purpose leaves the distribution notice conditions in place.

sources.locator: Noncommercial Organizations, Distribution License and Notices

scenarios.situation: Moving a no-charge prototype into a paid service
scenarios.text: Reassess the actual purpose before relying on this grant. A project with an anticipated commercial application falls outside the stated personal-use clause, even if the prototype has no price. Assess other permitted-purpose grounds, separate permission and any acts that require a copyright license. Whether the service distributes a copy is a separate factual question.
